item.research_question: How can a computationally efficient framework be developed to explore Pareto-optimal compositions and decipher trade-off relationships between strength and ductility in multi-component refractory alloys?
item.material_system: Refractory multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) based on Mo, Nb, Ti, Ta, W, Cr, Zr, Hf, and V (specifically MoNbTi and MoNbTiTa systems)
item.processing_route: Integration of Coherent Potential Approximation (CPA) for elastic constants and misfit volumes, actively learned Moment Tensor Potentials (MTP) for surface and unstable stacking fault energies, and a Virtual Bond Approximation (VBA) analytical model within a Bayesian multi-objective optimization workflow using NSGA-II
item.test_conditions: Search space constrained to 0.0 ≤ ci ≤ 0.75 for most components (Ti ≤ 0.55); evaluation of properties at ambient conditions via first-principles calculations and analytical models
key_findings: The strength of Pareto-optimal MoNbTi alloys ranges from ~50 MPa to ~260 MPa, with ductility index D changing from 1.23 to 1.35.
The addition of Ta to MoNbTi creates a disjoint Pareto set (PFA2) with strength >250 MPa, distinct from the MoNbTi(Ta) region (PFA1).
Surface energy convergence for MoNbTi requires up to 100 atomic layers, whereas typical SQS supercells (~100 atoms) yield errors of 10–20%.
The VBA model reproduces direct CPA+MTP calculations with high accuracy, capturing trends across the entire composition space using only element-specific bandwidths and d-electron counts.
Pearson correlation between predicted ductility index and measured fracture strain is -0.67, correctly ranking alloys at brittle and ductile extremes.
Alloys rich in Ti, Zr, and Nb form a distinct cluster with CRSS 200–400 MPa, while Ta- and W-rich alloys form a separate cluster with higher D values.
The misfit parameter δ and shear modulus G are the primary drivers for CRSS, while surface energy and USF energy govern the ductility index D.
item.mechanism: The framework leverages CPA's efficiency for properties insensitive to local relaxations (elastic constants, misfit volumes) and MTP's ability to handle local atomic relaxations for defects (surfaces, USFs). The VBA model extrapolates these trends using universal functions of d-valence and element-specific bandwidths, allowing the identification of optimal trade-offs where strength is tuned via misfit volume and ductility via surface energy.
item.limitations: The VBA model cannot replicate strong non-linear effects caused by Fermi-surface transitions (e.g., due to Ta), and the ductility index D does not account for intergranular fracture or grain boundary segregation.
item.future_work: The methodology can be extended to other mechanical properties like precipitation strengthening, and the VBA model can serve as a surrogate in multi-fidelity optimization frameworks to trigger rare ab initio evaluations.
quotes: We present a framework to explore Pareto-optimal compositions by integrating advanced ab initio-based techniques into a Bayesian multi-objective optimization workflow.
Our MTP approach yields values of 730 mJ/m2 and 853 mJ/m2, for {110} and {112} respectively.
In the case of MoNbTi, up to 100 layers are required to produce the correct (converged) values.

item.research_question: How can a computational framework be constructed to decipher trade-off relationships between intrinsic ductility and yield strength in multi-component alloys, specifically for MoNbTi and MoNbTiTa systems?
item.material_system: MoNbTi and MoNbTiTa refractory alloys; elemental compounds and selected binary, three- and four-component alloys
item.processing_route: Integration of Moment Tensor Potentials (MTPs) trained via active learning on DFT data; Multi-objective Bayesian optimization using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) and NSGAII; Virtual Bond Approximation (VBA) parameterization via CPA calculations; t-SNE dimensionality reduction for visualization
item.test_conditions: DFT computations with PBE functional, 400 eV energy cutoff, 0.15 Å⁻¹ k-point spacing, 0.08 eV Gaussian smearing; MD simulations at 50K, 150K, and 300K; Yield stress calculations assuming strain rate of 5 ⋅ 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ and reference rate of 10⁴ s⁻¹
key_findings: Initial training sets contained 146 and 377 configurations for MoNbTi and MoNbTiTa, respectively, which grew to 381 and 720 configurations after active learning and MD simulations.
Final training set errors for total energies were 6 meV/atom and 19 meV/atom, and for forces 0.099 and 0.104 eV/Å for MoNbTi and MoNbTiTa potentials.
The Bayesian optimization required 36 points for MoNbTi and 143 points for MoNbTiTa (split into two sets of 72 and 71) to converge on the Pareto front.

The Virtual Bond Approximation model was parameterized using CPA calculations for elemental compounds and binary alloys, then adjusted to align with relaxed surface and USF energies of individual elemental compounds.
The ductility index D is defined such that intrinsic ductility is achieved for D < 1 at T = 0K based on the ratio of stress intensity factors for cleavage and dislocation emission.
item.mechanism: The framework balances the competition between brittle cleavage (characterized by KIc) and ductile dislocation emission (characterized by KIe) at the crack tip to determine the ductility index. Yield strength is modeled using thermal activation models for solid solution strengthening, while the Virtual Bond Approximation provides a consistent characterization of thermodynamic and elastic properties derived from free energy derivatives.
item.limitations: The t-SNE projection provides only an approximate preservation of local structure and distances, leading to an observed patchy pattern. The analytical model for intrinsic ductility is limited to mode I loading. The yield strength model assumes dominating solid solution strengthening and requires subtracting an estimated Hall-Petch contribution from experimental data.
item.future_work: Integration of recently developed multicomponent magnetic MTPs into the framework to treat magnetic alloys with complex magnetic configurations. Complementing the approach with on-the-fly learning of MLIPs to broaden applicability to systems barely tractable by conventional Kohn-Sham DFT, such as isolated dislocations.
quotes: Another prospective direction for development is the integration of recently developed multicomponent magnetic MTPs into the presented framework, opening the possibility to treat magnetic alloys with complex magnetic configurations.
We only consider in our investigation mode I loading (stress orthogonal to the local plane of the crack surface), which generally limits the ductility the most.
The errors on the final training set for total energies are found to be 6 and 19 meV/atom, and for forces – 0.099 and 0.104 eV/Å for the MoNbTi and MoNbTiTa potentials, respectively.
